title: All-team orchestration & rotation playbook — Q2 prep
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the single-source working playbook for the company-wide Q2 preparation cycle: draft OKRs for the company update, the executive slide narrative, and the operational staffing/rotation plan for the all-team sync + two-week surge.

Audience:
- Execs (CEO, COO, CTO) for narrative and decisioning
- People Ops / Recruiting for staffing decisions
- Eng leads / Product / CS for commitment to OKR targets
- All-team ops + On-call rotation leads (SRE, Support)

High-level goals for this playbook (what we want by the sync):
- Finalize three company objectives and 6–9 measurable KRs (draft to in_review)
- Agree on run-of-show + timing for 90-minute all-team sync and breakouts
- Confirm staffing rotation for 2-week post-sync surge (oncall, pager coverage, CS escalations)
- Produce 1-page exec update and 10-slide narrative for CEO/CTO

OKR Drafts (company-level) — working numbers, metrics to validate: 
Objective A — Make inference predictable and cheaper for customers
- KR1: Reduce avg cost-per-1M-token served by 18% vs baseline (baseline = Jan 2026)
- KR2: 95th-percentile API latency <= 180ms for hosted tier (P95 measured across last 30d)
- KR3: Apply intelligent routing to 60% of eligible requests (measured by route decisions)

Objective B — Expand enterprise adoption of Dedicated and Private modes
- KR1: Sign 6 new Dedicated contracts (>= $100k ARR each)
- KR2: Complete 2 private on-prem pilots with compliance artifacts (SOC/ISO starter pack)
- KR3: Increase POC->paid conversion rate from Dedicated trials to 25%

Objective C — Developer-first operational tooling and observability
- KR1: Ship token cost breakdown per-route in Console for 100% of customer routes
- KR2: Launch rollout manager alpha and run 3 canary rollouts successfully
- KR3: Automate 30% of performance regressions detection (alerts tied to evals)

Notes on OKR numbers: these are intentionally aggressive — product & eng leads, please sanity-check capacity and expected lift before the exec review. Tag metrics that require infra changes (e.g., P95 target) so SRE can sign off.

Executive update / slide narrative (10 slides) — rough outline:
1) Cover (Title, date, CEO)
2) State of platform — short metrics snapshot (latency, costs, availability, revenue signals)
3) Where we are vs last quarter (wins + regressions)
4) Company objectives proposed (one slide with 3 objectives)
5) Why these objectives — short thesis (market + product alignment)
6) Execution plan highlights (serving runtime improvements, routing, Dedicated motion)
7) Customer stories / signal (2–3 bullets with anonymized metrics)
8) Risks & mitigations (capacity, hiring, regulatory)
9) Ask of the company (focus areas and how teams should align)
10) Logistics / Q&A run-of-show for the all-team sync

Run-of-show (90 minutes) — proposed timing (T = 0 start)
- T+0: CEO opening (8 min): anchor statement, top 2 company priorities
- T+8: CTO technical narrative (10 min): runtime wins, quantized roadmap and capacity picture
- T+18: Product lead (8 min): customer use cases, Dedicated pipeline status
- T+26: Metrics snapshot & OKR ask (8 min): present the three objectives and KRs
- T+34: Short customer video or readout (3 min) + transition
- T+38: Breakouts (3 concurrent tracks, 30 minutes):
  * Track A: Hosting & Latency (eng + SRE + infra)
  * Track B: Enterprise & Dedicated (sales + solutions + legal)
  * Track C: Developer tooling & Console (DX + product)
- T+68: Breakout report-backs (15 min) — 5 min per track
- T+83: Leadership closing & next steps (7 min)

Breakout goals (each): deliver 3 committed next steps, with owners and timelines (1–2 week near-term actions).

Staffing rotation & surge plan (two-week window after sync) — objectives:
- Ensure 24/7 critical coverage for any Dedicated/Private onboarding failures
- Provide SLA-grade escalation capacity for Hosted customers while we push platform changes
- Keep engineering momentum while preventing burnout with structured rotations

Proposed rotation (example roster for week 1 & 2):
- Core SRE oncall: 1 primary, 1 secondary per 24h block (teams pool across regions)
- Support escalation engineer: Mon–Fri 9a–6p core, 1 engineer on rotation evenings + weekend on-call
- Console/Deploy lead: 1 daytime rota to own rollouts and rollback authority
- Exec escalation contact: VP Eng (on-call schedule posted)

Staggering approach (minimize single point of failure):
- Teams rotate in 4-day blocks (A/B/C/D) so that no one is oncall > 6 days straight across surge
- Recruiting will push temp contractors for customer-facing triage for high-volume windows

Communications plan (internal + external):
- Internal: #all-hands-summary Slack thread with TL;DR + breakouts notes. Daily surge standup at 9:30am for first week.
- External: Notice to Dedicated customers 48h before any disruptive rollout; CS account leads to own outbound comms for major customers.

Prep checklist (owners called out) — must be completed 48h before the sync:
- Finalize slides + rehearse (CEO + CTO) — Owner: Maya Thompson (deadline: T-2 days)
- Confirm breakouts and facilitators — Owner: Leila Morgan (T-3 days)
- Publish rotating roster + escalation matrix — Owner: Rajiv Kapoor (T-4 days)
- QA & deploy safety net (rollback steps documented) — Owner: Carlos Jimenez (T-2 days)
- Run dress rehearsal with AV/test streaming — Owner: Events Ops (T-1 day)

Risks & open questions (notes to execs):
- Capacity risk: if Dedicated conversions exceed projections, we need to reorder infra priorities — SRE signoff required for KR feasibility.
- Measurement risk: some KRs depend on new routing telemetry that is only in alpha — is it acceptable to show provisional numbers?
- People risk: staging high-priority rollouts during hiring freeze weeks could cause resourcing gaps.

Decision requests for execs (short list):
1) Approve go-forward OKR targets as listed (or flag which KRs need relaxation)
2) Approve two-week surge budget for temp CS headcount (estimate: $18k)
3) Confirm exec presence and time allocation for the all-team sync

Appendix / artifacts to attach (working):
- Draft slides (link: https://drive.redwood/drafts/q2-exec-slides)
- Ledger of recent regressions & mitigations (JIRA:REG-101..REG-120)
- Capacity model snapshot (sheet link in linked_artifacts)

Editor's notes / rough TODOs (incomplete sentences ok):
- Need SRE to provide updated P95 calcs by EOD Friday — Rajiv to ping SRE leads.
- Maya to draft CEO opening paragraph, keep it tight & <200 words.
- Decide whether to surface cost per-token benchmarking publicly in the all-team deck or keep to exec appendix.

Lower-priority ideas for future cycles (parking lot):
- Standardize rotation templates per team for faster staffing plan generation
- Expand Console guided runbooks for Dedicated onboards
- Small cross-team tabletop drills for deployment rollbacks

End of playbook (working).

-- Leila (notes: share with execs + leads; will iterate after lead signoffs)
